transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood), Daniel Hsu (Meridian), Laura Perez (Meridian), Ibrahim Malik (Meridian), Sofia Alvarez (Meridian)

Summary: discovery focused on Dedicated (reserved GPU) option for Meridian Bank's document understanding and chat assistant workloads. Topics: reserved capacity, isolation (VPC/on-prem), burst/overflow strategy, expected throughput, latency vs cost tradeoffs, security controls (KMS, SOC2, audit logs), next steps and benchmarks.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we scheduled 55 minutes, appreciate you carving this out. quick intros?
[00:18] Daniel Hsu: yeah hi, Daniel here, head of MLOps at Meridian, we run a bunch of document ingestion pipelines, looking at inference infra for customer-facing assistants.
[00:30] Laura Perez: Laura, VP Eng, overseeing platform and ops. main ask is predictability and isolation for PII workloads.
[00:40] Ibrahim Malik: Ibrahim, security architect, I'll be leading compliance review.
[00:48] Alex Chen: awesome. Priya, you want to frame what we'll cover?
[00:53] Priya Nair: sure, we'll walk through dedicated capacity model, sizing heuristics, burst strategy / overflow to hosted, networking and KMS, and then align on a benchmark plan. obvious caveats: seaming and small transcription issues in this call, so sorry if things are fuzzy.
[01:10] Sofia Alvarez: quick note - timeline is Q2 pilot ideally, production H2 if all goes well.
[01:18] Alex Chen: great. can you give baseline numbers: concurrency, token sizes, typical qps?
[01:25] Daniel Hsu: yes, so we have two main workloads - chat assistant (avg 150 tokens/response, 10-15 tokens/sec generation) and doc-extract (batch, longer sequences up to 2k tokens). Target is ~200 rps peak for chat, but most requests are low RPS with spikes.
[01:45] Laura Perez: and SLOs we care about: 95th latency under 300ms for short chat, 99th under 1s would be ideal. cost target obviously under current cloud spend for managed endpoints.
[02:02] Priya Nair: ok, that maps to dedicated usage - reserved GPUs can give predictable throughput and lower unit cost. couple of clarifying q's: what models are you intending to run? open models or internal fine-tuned LLMs?
[02:16] Daniel Hsu: open models mainly, we have a fine-tuned Flume-2 variant and a separate BERT-ish reranker, and we'll probably push some 7B/13B families into prod. we can share artifacts for the benchmark.
[02:30] Priya Nair: perfect. on dedicated we usually size by token throughput and concurrency; for 13B LLMs, ballpark 40-60 tok/ms? (note: numbers approximate, we will bench). are you expecting continuous baseline traffic or mostly bursty?
[02:49] Daniel Hsu: baseline low (maybe 30-50 qps), but burst to 200 during business hours. need reserve for baseline and autoscale for burst, without compromising isolation.
[03:05] Alex Chen: key thing: Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools (you get capacity isolation), and we offer burst capacity options that let you overflow to hosted when reserved is saturated.
[03:17] Ibrahim Malik: how does overflow work from security perspective? data residency and encryption are concerns.
[03:24] Priya Nair: good question — overflow can be configured so that PII or flagged requests never leave your VPC; you can set routing policies by tag. for other traffic we can overflow to Redwood-hosted but we can also provision burst on the same tenancy if you want fully private bursts (that's a contractual/infra choice).
[03:44] Laura Perez: what about peering and network egress - we have strict egress controls.
[03:50] Priya Nair: we support VPC peering and private link; our Private control plane or Dedicated placement can live in your VPC; for hosted overflow you'd need to allow specific egress ranges. we'll share network topologies.
[04:03] Daniel Hsu: CPU/GPU ratio — we'll run some lightweight preprocessors on host. how is co-tenancy handled? we need strong tenant isolation.
[04:13] Alex Chen: Dedicated means your GPUs aren't shared with other customers; control plane is multi-tenant but data plane isolation and network isolation are configurable. for stricter needs we have Private deployments or on-prem appliances.
[04:28] Priya Nair: also note we provide audit logs per-request and token-level lineage. Ibrahim, this ties to KMS and HSM integration too.
[04:38] Ibrahim Malik: KMS — we use cloud KMS and HSM for keys; can Redwood integrate with our KMS and rotate keys on schedule?
[04:47] Priya Nair: yes - Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS. HSM integrations are possible for Private/on-prem. key rotation and envelope encryption supported. we'll share doc with exact flows.
[04:58] Sofia Alvarez: on billing, would dedicated be flat monthly plus usage or purely committed RU?
[05:05] Alex Chen: reserved capacity is commit-based (monthly/annual) with a baseline commit and optional burst billing on top. we can model different commit levels; we typically show TCO comparisons vs hosted endpoints.
[05:18] Laura Perez: how do you measure throughput per GPU? we need to know how many GPUs to reserve for our 200 rps burst.
[05:25] Priya Nair: we'll run model-specific benches but rough math: for a 13B model on an A100-class GPU, you might get X concurrency — (note: we'll validate). we prefer to run a live bench with your model artifacts to provide accurate numbers.
[05:40] Daniel Hsu: can we run canary/rollouts across model versions? need ability to pin versions and fallback.
[05:47] Alex Chen: yes - rollouts, canaries and automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant are supported in Redwood Console. you can pin versions per route, and configure automatic fallback rules.
[05:58] Ibrahim Malik: audit and compliance - do you provide per-route audit logs and retention controls? we have retention policies of 7 years for some logs.
[06:07] Priya Nair: yes audit logs are available, retention configurable as an add-on. SOC2 and ISO attestations are in our security pack. we'll attach the reports.
[06:16] Laura Perez: any limitations on custom quantized models? we sometimes want to run int8 quantized variants.
[06:23] Priya Nair: supported — quantization profiles are managed; we have recommended quant configs and can help validate accuracy regressions with evals. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization tradeoffs per workload.
[06:36] Alex Chen: want to talk about burst strategy: options are (1) pre-provision extra reserved capacity to cover spikes, (2) autoscale within your reserved pool if you have spare capacity, or (3) overflow to hosted or a private burst pool. each comes with tradeoffs on cost and latency.
[06:54] Daniel Hsu: latency matters for chat. overflow to hosted adds network hop — how much penalty?
[07:02] Priya Nair: depends on region and VPC peering; typical added latency might be 40-120ms if crossing to hosted. for most chat use-cases that keeps 95th under 300ms, but we'll measure.
[07:16] Laura Perez: we'd prefer private burst if price delta isn't huge. can you quantify costs for private burst?
[07:23] Alex Chen: yes, we'll include private burst pricing in the proposal. usually private bursts are more expensive than reserved but cheaper than full hosted ops at scale because of reserved amortization.
[07:35] Sofia Alvarez: security question — can we restrict which models can overflow? ex: PII flagged requests never overflow.
[07:43] Priya Nair: absolutely. routing policies can tag requests and route based on rules; you can block overflow for flagged classes.
[07:50] Daniel Hsu: okay, for benching we'll want to simulate bursts and also long-seq doc extraction. what metrics do you usually capture?
[07:58] Priya Nair: throughput (rps), latency p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, token/sec, memory usage, failure rates, and cold-start times for KV cache warmups. we also capture cost-per-1k-tokens.
[08:12] Laura Perez: about KV cache — we use long conversations and want KV cache to persist across requests. how does that work in dedicated?
[08:20] Priya Nair: KV cache is per-session; we support sticky routing and cache sharing across GPUs in the same pool. we can pre-warm KV cache for expected sessions to prevent cold-start latencies. note: K-V cache transcribed sometimes as K-V cash in auto transcripts.
[08:35] Ibrahim Malik: encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between our services and your data plane?
[08:41] Alex Chen: yes, mTLS supported along with mutual auth.
[08:45] Daniel Hsu: any limits on concurrent streams for streaming responses?
[08:49] Priya Nair: streaming is supported; concurrent stream limits are tied to connection limits per node; we can provision nodes for high concurrency streaming workloads.
[09:00] Alex Chen: let's pivot to pilot design: we recommend a 4-week pilot with 2 phases — Phase 1: functional correctness + small perf tests; Phase 2: scale and burst bench with traffic replay.
[09:12] Daniel Hsu: sounds good. what artifacts do you need from us?
[09:17] Priya Nair: model artifacts, sample prompts, representative traffic traces (anonymized), network peering info, and a list of PII flags/labels.
[09:25] Laura Perez: timeline - can you run the bench week of 1/26?
[09:30] Alex Chen: yes, we'll target that. we'll also include a pricing proposal showing reserved tiers and burst addons.
[09:36] Sofia Alvarez: another question: are there SLA options for dedicated (uptime/latency)?
[09:41] Alex Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency objectives as part of reserved contracts; we can discuss enterprise SLA tiers.
[09:49] Ibrahim Malik: vendor management — will you sign our standard DPA?
[09:53] Alex Chen: we have standard DPA and can negotiate enterprise DPA for large deals.
[09:58] Priya Nair: just to call out — sometimes people compare to Bedrock or Anthropic. the differentiation we're highlighting is production controls (caching, batching, routing, observability) and cost optimizations.
[10:12] Daniel Hsu: noted. one more - how do upgrades to model runtime impact existing traffic?
[10:18] Priya Nair: we support rolling upgrades with canary traffic and automatic rollback on regressions; you can pin versions to avoid automatic rollout.
[10:26] Alex Chen: ok, going to do a quick recap and next steps in the last ~2 minutes.
[10:30] -- (call continues with deeper technical Qs; for brevity, later sections paraphrased) --
[28:15] Priya Nair: dug into quantization and inference kernels — we can load quant profiles and validate quality with your eval set, Redwood Optimize can run automated regressions.
[34:40] Daniel Hsu: good to know. also need support window — 24/7 for production?
[34:46] Alex Chen: we offer premium 24/7 support as an add-on for Dedicated and Private customers.
[38:02] Priya Nair: on autoscaling, Dedicated supports configured autoscale policies (grow/shrink nodes) with cooldowns; but autoscale speed depends on model cold-starts and KV cache warming.
[41:10] Laura Perez: what's the expected warmup time for long-seq doc runs?
[41:16] Priya Nair: it depends on model and KV cache but typical pre-warm 30-90s to get steady-state throughput for very long sequences.
[45:00] Daniel Hsu: ok, security follow-ups — Ibrahim will send SOC/PCI questions.
[45:07] Ibrahim Malik: yes, I'll compile and share next week.
[50:20] Alex Chen: thanks everyone - we'll send the pricing, security pack, and a benchmark plan. can we tentatively book the bench week of 2026-01-26?
[50:30] Laura Perez: yes that's fine.
[50:35] Alex Chen: great, recap of next steps: pricing, SOC2 docs, benchmark plan + artifacts, schedule bench. action items logged.
[50:50] Daniel Hsu: thanks, talk soon.
[50:55] Alex Chen: thanks all, bye.
